The explanation's physics is correct. In a DC machine with brushes and a commutator, the rotor is the armature (電機子). Armature reaction shifts the electrical neutral axis away from the geometric neutral axis. If the brushes are not moved to follow it, commutation fails and sparks (火花) form. Compensating windings (補償巻線) are mainly used in large machines, and interpoles (補極) are the usual choice in small machines.

The explanation's physics is correct. The damper winding (制動巻線) is a squirrel-cage conductor, so the machine starts on the same principle as a squirrel-cage induction motor. To protect insulation from the high voltage induced during starting, the field winding is short-circuited through a resistor. Near synchronous speed the short is removed and DC excitation pulls the rotor into synchronism.
